prompt: Which of the following best explains why the question of slavery in the territories became increasingly divisive between 1846 and 1860?
teacher_notes: Ask students to place the Wilmot Proviso, the Compromise of 1850, and the Kansas-Nebraska Act on a timeline to see the pattern of repeated reopening.

choices: Territorial expansion after the Mexican-American War forced Congress to decide the status of slavery in newly acquired land
The invention of the cotton gin made slavery unprofitable across the South
Immigration from Ireland and Germany eliminated sectional differences over labor
The Supreme Court refused to hear any case involving enslaved people

explanation: Victory in the Mexican-American War added vast territory, and every attempt to organize it, from the Wilmot Proviso through the Compromise of 1850 to the Kansas-Nebraska Act, reopened the question of whether slavery would expand. The cotton gin made slavery more profitable, not less; immigration intensified rather than resolved labor tensions; and the Court did rule on such cases, most consequentially in Dred Scott v. Sandford in 1857.
